items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1969-12-04
items.q: So I told Mr. Cobb, I want to know who he'd wear them. I practically ran that joint because he knew nothing about it.

ctx.x: Where you been? Well, he said, it's only so he made a table. It got so we didn't have enough tables and the head waiter started making all the money. Because my friends would say, you asked me to come. He tells me I don't have a table. And I had made the reservations for them. So I told Mr. Cobb, I want to know who he'd wear them. I practically ran that joint because he knew nothing about it. All he did was sit there and smoke, chain smoking cigars, you know. Fine man, finest. Could have lost a short, I waited…

There was a trumpet player there that I never have been able to find much about. And I thought maybe he was there right before you or right after you. Did you know Frank Garante? He was from Italy. Frank who?

items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1973-03-16
items.q: because Mr. Cobb had been after me for a couple of years, we stayed with Mr. Cobb seven years.

ctx.x: Okay. The question was what, about your first band?

I organized my band in 1917. The play at a hotel in Atlantic City. When the war came on, the contract was cancelled. So I played a little jazz at the Orphan Theater, and Mr. Grunlong happened to be in the audience, and he heard us. He waited for me, and he said, they tell me you have a band. I said, yes. He said, could I hear it? I said, let's play him. So we made an audition. We played two numbers. He okayed the orchestra, sent us to get uniforms, and we stayed with him four solid years in the cave and in the…
